newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan president vows to fight China's "repression".
newsitem.headline: Taiwan president vows to fight China's "repression".

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui has accused China of "senseless repression" and said his island would continue to seek international recognition despite recently losing its biggest ally, South Africa, to Beijing.

Lee, commenting for the first time on Pretoria's plan to switch diplomatic recognition from Taipei to Beijing by the end of 1997, said Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government would continue to seek an international role.

"Although the Republic of China has suffered from communist China's senseless repression diplomatically, we will never set limits for ourselves," Lee said in an address made late on Friday and carried by state television on Saturday.
"We will continue to participate in international affairs according to the ideal of promoting our country's development and existence," he said.
Pretoria's announcement on Wednesday was the biggest blow to Taipei's ongoing efforts to break out of a Beijing-imposed isolation since South Korea switched diplomatic ties to China in 1992.
China regards Taiwan as a renegade province not entitled to international recognition since the two split after a civil war in 1949.
Beijing, which threatens to attack Taiwan if it tries to declare independence, intensified its containment policy after Lee made a private, but high-profile visit to the U.S. in 1995.

China mounted intimidating war games in waters near Taiwan in the months leading up to the island's March presidential election, which Lee won in a landslide, and has stepped up pressure on South Africa and other diplomatic allies of Taiwan to switch ties to Beijing.
South Africa is the biggest of only 30 countries -- mostly underdeveloped states in central America and Africa -- that recognise Taiwan rather than the communist People's Republic on the mainland.
Taipei has blamed its fallout with Pretoria on Beijing and said it would not launch further steps to boost economic ties with China.
Some 25,000 Taiwan businesses have poured over US$20 billion into the Chinese mainland, making Taiwan one of the leading overseas investors in China.
